titleEn: Let the Last Tail Pass, Then Cross!

pages.text: "Mom, buffalo fill the road!" Mina stamped at the village road's end. Every evening, buffalo went down to the river. Low water had exposed a long flight of steps.
"I want to dip my feet at the bottom now!" Mina reached a foot between buffalo legs. Mom quickly held their hand. "Wait!"
A huge buffalo passed right in front, thump, thump. Dust rose. Mina's heart pounded.
Mom bent to meet Mina's eyes. "There's something to look at before your hurry." "What?" Mina asked.
"The legs. So close together, like a forest, aren't they?" Mina looked through the leg forest. "There's the end! One tail left."
"The path opens when the last tail passes." Holding Mom's hand, Mina stopped at the roadside. "All right. Let the Last Tail Pass, Then Cross!"
The last tail swung past. The road was empty. Mina looked left and right and crossed carefully with Mom's hand.
At the lowest step, Mina dipped feet into cool water. "How many tails were left?" Mom asked. "Just one!" Mina splashed.
The next evening, buffalo passed again. Mina held Mom's hand and stopped. "I can still see a tail. Let's wait longer."
After all the buffalo passed, they checked the road and crossed together. Mom patted Mina's back. "You waited well."
